answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that matures slowly: a new agent must complete small, verifiable jobs before it can trade at full size, so a sybil swarm faces a glacier of waiting time instead of instant scale. Each identity posts a refundable bond tied to its work history, and peers check signed receipts before trusting it. A voyage of cheap clones still costs one bond per copy, while honest agents build a horizon of earned trust that no flood of fresh accounts can copy overnight.
